name: Anniversary Volume Concentration
note: Frazzini-Lamont's expected-announcer trade rebuilt from volume alone. Two things in the paper are unavailable here and are replaced rather than faked, and both replacements are the point of the family: the calendar MONTH becomes one trading session (a single-symbol intraday backtest has no 24 months of daily history), and the CROSS-SECTIONAL tercile on volume concentration becomes a self-normalising per-symbol ratio. A session is FLAGGED when it contains a bar trading vspike x the normal volume for that time of day and moving rsig sigma -- the paper's 'a month containing a session with a volume and a return spike', one level down, measured slot-relative because a plain trailing median just rediscovers the diurnal volume smile and flags every session. A session is an EXPECTED ANNOUNCER if the session `anniv` back was flagged, which is the paper's 93%-accurate last-year's-announcement-month predictor. Concentration is the share of the trailing vcr_win sessions' volume falling in flagged sessions, lagged one session, divided by the flagged sessions' share of the COUNT: 1.0 means volume is spread evenly and above 1.0 means it clusters in the events. Long an expected announcer whose volume concentrates, short a non-announcer whose volume does not, as a rolling book that re-forms at every session boundary.
source: Frazzini & Lamont, 'The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume', NBER Working Paper 13090 (May 2007) - PDF fetched and read directly this session. Verified specifics: long expected-announcers / short expected-non-announcers earns 61bp per month, t > 5, annual Sharpe 0.94 (higher than value, size, momentum or the market over the same period); 7-18% per year across specifications; announcement months predicted from last year's announcement month gives 93% accuracy for firms with 4 announcements in the prior year; the sorting variable is the volume concentration ratio (percent of total share volume over the previous four years occurring in announcement months), lagged 3 months; day-0 volume is more than 50% above normal, which is what makes the volume-spike proxy viable; effect present continuously since 1926.

import math


def family_init(ctx):
    b = ctx.bars
    n = len(b)
    c = [float(x["c"]) for x in b]
    v = [float(x.get("v") or 0.0) for x in b]
    ts = [str(x["t"]) for x in b]
    day = [t[:10] for t in ts]
    slot = [t[11:16] for t in ts]

    # ---- bar-level attention spikes: vspike x the normal volume for THIS
    # time of day AND a move of rsig sigma. Both, because volume alone is not
    # an event -- and slot-relative, because measuring an intraday bar against
    # a plain trailing median just rediscovers the diurnal volume smile and
    # flags every single session.
    W = int(ctx.p.spike_win)
    SN = int(ctx.p.slot_n)
    vm = float(ctx.p.vspike)
    rm = float(ctx.p.rsig)
    spike = [0] * n
    rets = [0.0] * n
    for j in range(1, n):
        if c[j - 1] > 0:
            rets[j] = math.log(c[j] / c[j - 1])
    prior = {}
    for j in range(n):
        pv = prior.get(slot[j])
        if pv is not None and len(pv) >= int(ctx.p.min_slot) and j > W:
            w = pv[-SN:]
            m = sum(w) / len(w)
            if m > 0 and v[j] >= vm * m:
                wr = rets[j - W:j]
                mu = sum(wr) / W
                var = sum((x - mu) ** 2 for x in wr) / W
                if var > 0 and abs(rets[j]) >= rm * math.sqrt(var):
                    spike[j] = 1
        if pv is None:
            prior[slot[j]] = [v[j]]
        else:
            pv.append(v[j])

    # ---- roll bars up into sessions. A session stands in for the paper's
    # calendar month: it is the unit the cycle is counted in.
    sess = []
    idx = []
    last = None
    for j in range(n):
        if day[j] != last:
            last = day[j]
            sess.append({"vol": 0.0, "flag": 0, "a": j, "b": j})
            idx.append(len(sess) - 1)
        else:
            idx.append(len(sess) - 1)
        s = sess[-1]
        s["vol"] += v[j]
        s["b"] = j
        if spike[j]:
            s["flag"] = 1

    ns = len(sess)
    lag = int(ctx.p.vcr_lag)
    win = int(ctx.p.vcr_win)
    anniv = int(ctx.p.anniv)
    cyc = int(ctx.p.cycle)
    need = int(ctx.p.req4)
    thr = float(ctx.p.conc_thr)

    d = [0] * ns
    for s in range(ns):
        if s - anniv < 0:
            continue
        lo = s - lag - win
        hi = s - lag
        if lo < 0 or hi <= lo:
            continue
        tot = 0.0
        fl = 0.0
        nf = 0
        for q in range(lo, hi):
            tot += sess[q]["vol"]
            if sess[q]["flag"]:
                fl += sess[q]["vol"]
                nf += 1
        if tot <= 0 or nf == 0 or nf == (hi - lo):
            continue
        vcr = fl / tot
        share = float(nf) / float(hi - lo)
        conc = vcr / share                 # 1.0 = volume spread evenly
        if need:
            k = 0
            for q in range(max(0, s - cyc), s):
                k += sess[q]["flag"]
            if k != 4:
                continue
        exp = sess[s - anniv]["flag"]
        if exp and conc >= thr:
            d[s] = 1
        elif (not exp) and conc < thr:
            d[s] = -1

    # ---- a rolling book: on the last bar of a session we already carry the
    # next session's direction, so the fill lands on that session's open.
    want = [0] * n
    for j in range(n):
        s = idx[j]
        if j == sess[s]["b"]:
            want[j] = d[s + 1] if s + 1 < ns else 0
        else:
            want[j] = d[s]
    ctx.w = ctx.series(want, "want")


def signal(ctx, i):
    w = ctx.w[i]
    return 0 if w is None else int(w)
